title: Fast Thermalization With Quantum Algorithms
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 03 July 2026;
tldr: A quantum algorithm efficiently prepares thermal equilibrium states, advancing quantum simulation of thermodynamics.
motivation: Preparing thermal states is crucial for quantum simulation of many-body systems, but existing methods are inefficient.
method: The algorithm uses a combination of Hamiltonian simulation and quantum signal processing to prepare Gibbs states with provable efficiency.
result: The algorithm achieves polynomial scaling in system size and inverse temperature, outperforming previous approaches.
conclusion: This work provides a practical quantum algorithm for thermal state preparation, enabling new applications in quantum thermodynamics and condensed matter physics.

title: Learning Pure Quantum States Almost Without Regret
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: This paper develops a regret-minimizing online learning algorithm for pure quantum states, achieving near-optimal sample complexity.
motivation: Learning unknown quantum states efficiently is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods often require many copies or assume prior knowledge. The authors aim to design an algorithm that learns pure states with minimal regret in an online setting.
method: The authors propose a Bayesian approach using a Dirichlet prior over the Bloch sphere and derive a posterior update rule. They analyze the regret using information-theoretic tools and show that the algorithm achieves O(√T) regret, matching a lower bound.
result: The algorithm achieves a regret bound of O(√T) for learning pure states, which is optimal up to logarithmic factors. Numerical simulations confirm the theoretical predictions.
conclusion: The work provides a principled online learning framework for pure quantum states, with implications for quantum tomography and adaptive measurement strategies.

title: Gradiometric, Fully Tunable C-shunted Flux Qubits
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 02 July 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a gradiometric, fully tunable C-shunted flux qubit design that improves coherence and tunability for quantum computing applications.
motivation: Flux qubits suffer from sensitivity to flux noise and limited tunability, which hinders their performance in quantum processors. A design that mitigates these issues is needed.
method: The authors introduce a gradiometric design with a C-shunt capacitor to reduce flux noise sensitivity and enable full tunability of the qubit frequency. They fabricate and characterize the device at millikelvin temperatures.
result: The qubit exhibits improved coherence times (T1, T2) compared to standard flux qubits, and its frequency can be tuned over a wide range without significant degradation.
conclusion: The gradiometric C-shunted flux qubit is a promising platform for scalable quantum computing due to its enhanced coherence and tunability.

title: Magnon Fluctuations Find A Structure
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 30 June 2026;
tldr: Observation of magnon squeezing in magnetic insulators driven into a non-equilibrium state.
motivation: To understand and control magnon fluctuations in non-equilibrium magnetic systems, which is relevant to quantum thermodynamics and information processing.
method: Experimental observation of magnon squeezing in magnetic insulators under non-equilibrium driving conditions.
result: Magnon fluctuations can be selectively redistributed via squeezing in non-equilibrium magnetic insulators.
conclusion: The phenomenon of magnon squeezing provides a new way to manipulate quantum fluctuations in magnetic systems, with potential implications for quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Enhancing Classical Simulation With Noisy Quantum Devices
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 02 July 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes a method to enhance classical simulation of quantum circuits by leveraging noisy quantum devices, using a hybrid approach that combines classical and quantum resources.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is computationally expensive, and noisy quantum devices are currently limited. The authors aim to use noisy quantum devices to improve the efficiency of classical simulation.
method: The method involves running a quantum circuit on a noisy device, measuring the output, and using the measurement results to guide a classical simulation algorithm, effectively reducing the simulation cost.
result: The hybrid approach achieves a significant speedup over purely classical simulation for certain circuit classes, even when the quantum device has moderate noise levels.
conclusion: Noisy quantum devices can be valuable for enhancing classical simulation, providing a practical application for near-term quantum hardware.

title: A Context-aware Gate Set Tomography: Improving The Self-consistent Characterization Of Trapped-ion Universal Gate Sets By Leveraging non-Markovianity
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: This paper introduces a context-aware gate set tomography method that leverages non-Markovianity to improve the self-consistent characterization of trapped-ion universal gate sets.
motivation: Standard gate set tomography assumes Markovian noise, which is often violated in trapped-ion systems, leading to inaccurate characterization. The authors aim to develop a method that accounts for non-Markovian effects to obtain more reliable gate set estimates.
method: The authors propose a context-aware gate set tomography protocol that incorporates non-Markovian noise by using a hidden Markov model or similar framework to capture temporal correlations in the noise. They apply this to trapped-ion universal gate sets and compare performance against standard GST.
result: The context-aware method yields significantly improved accuracy in estimating gate fidelities and error rates compared to standard GST, especially under realistic non-Markovian noise conditions. The method also provides insights into the noise spectrum.
conclusion: Leveraging non-Markovianity in gate set tomography enables more self-consistent and accurate characterization of trapped-ion quantum gates, which is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Doubly-polylog-time-overhead Fault-tolerant Quantum Computation By A Polylog-time Parallel Minimum-weight Perfect Matching Decoder
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 02 July 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a fault-tolerant quantum computation scheme using a polylog-time parallel minimum-weight perfect matching decoder, achieving doubly-polylog-time overhead.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires efficient decoding algorithms to correct errors with low time overhead, which is crucial for practical quantum computers.
method: The authors develop a parallelized version of the minimum-weight perfect matching decoder that runs in polylogarithmic time, and integrate it into a fault-tolerant protocol with doubly-polylogarithmic time overhead.
result: The proposed decoder achieves polylog-time parallel decoding, and the overall fault-tolerant scheme has doubly-polylog-time overhead, improving over previous polynomial-time decoders.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that efficient parallel decoding can significantly reduce the time overhead of fault-tolerant quantum computation, bringing it closer to practical implementation.

title: A Framework Of Partial Error Correction For Intermediate-scale Quantum Computers
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 01 July 2026;
tldr: Proposes a framework for partial error correction tailored to near-term quantum computers, balancing error suppression and resource overhead.
motivation: Full quantum error correction is too resource-intensive for near-term devices; partial error correction can improve fidelity with manageable overhead.
method: Develops a theoretical framework that allows selective correction of errors based on their impact, using a combination of error detection and post-selection.
result: Demonstrates that partial error correction can significantly outperform no correction and sometimes approach full correction performance with fewer resources.
conclusion: Partial error correction is a practical strategy for intermediate-scale quantum computers, offering a trade-off between error suppression and resource cost.

title: Quantum State Design And Emergent Confinement Mechanism In Measured Tensor Network States
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 04 July 2026;
tldr: This paper studies the emergence of quantum state designs and confinement in monitored random tensor networks, linking measurement-induced phase transitions to entanglement dynamics.
motivation: Understanding the structure of quantum states generated by random unitary circuits with measurements is crucial for quantum information processing and many-body physics.
method: The authors analyze the spectral properties of the density matrix in a tensor network model with projective measurements, using replica methods and mapping to a classical statistical mechanics model.
result: They show that the system exhibits a confinement mechanism that leads to the formation of approximate quantum state designs in the volume-law phase, with a transition to a confined phase at high measurement rates.
conclusion: The work provides a new perspective on measurement-induced phase transitions and the emergence of randomness in quantum circuits, with implications for quantum error correction and thermalization.

title: Planar Fault-tolerant Logical Measurements With Low Qubit Overhead
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 30 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a method for fault-tolerant logical measurements on planar surface codes with reduced qubit overhead.
motivation: Fault-tolerant logical measurements are essential for quantum error correction, but existing methods often require high qubit overhead, limiting scalability.
method: The authors propose a planar architecture for logical measurements that uses fewer ancilla qubits by optimizing the measurement circuit and exploiting the planar geometry.
result: They demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves fault tolerance with significantly lower qubit overhead compared to standard approaches, while maintaining comparable error thresholds.
conclusion: This work advances practical quantum error correction by reducing resource requirements for logical measurements, bringing fault-tolerant quantum computing closer to realization.

title: Tangled Up In Spin
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 01 July 2026;
tldr: Neutron scattering measurements on a strongly correlated metal suggest quantum entanglement in the strange metal state.
motivation: To investigate whether quantum entanglement underlies the anomalous properties of strange metals.
method: Neutron scattering experiments on a strongly correlated metal.
result: Hints of quantum entanglement observed in the strange metal state.
conclusion: Quantum entanglement may play a role in strange metal behavior, but further study is needed.

title: An Integrated Theoretical And Numerical Approach To Understand Modern Experiments On Quantum Magnetism
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 29 June 2026;
tldr: This perspective article advocates for tighter collaboration between analytical theory, numerics, and experiments to advance the study of quantum magnetism.
motivation: Many exciting phenomena predicted by theories of quantum magnets have not yet been observed, highlighting a gap between theory and experiment.
method: The authors argue for an integrated approach combining analytical theory, numerical simulations, and experimental techniques.
result: No specific new results are presented; the paper is a perspective on methodology.
conclusion: Progress in quantum magnetism requires closer collaboration across theoretical, numerical, and experimental domains.

title: Surface d-orbital Order In An Intermetallic Compound
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 29 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reports the observation of surface d-orbital order in an intermetallic compound without structural or magnetic order.
motivation: The existence of orbital order with a clear band-structure fingerprint in correlated materials has been unresolved.
method: The authors used angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and other techniques to study the electronic structure of the intermetallic compound.
result: They observed an orbital order from rare earth 5d electrons that is not accompanied by structural or magnetic order.
conclusion: This finding demonstrates a new type of orbital order in intermetallic compounds, which may have implications for understanding correlated electron systems.

title: Organic Cocrystals Offer Record Photothermal Conversion
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 02 July 2026;
tldr: Organic cocrystals achieve record photothermal conversion via quantum coherent beating.
motivation: To enhance photothermal conversion efficiency in organic solids for applications like solar energy harvesting.
method: Design of centrosymmetric cocrystals that exploit quantum coherent beating to improve light-to-heat conversion.
result: Achieved the highest temperature recorded for organic solids under laser illumination.
conclusion: Quantum coherent beating in organic cocrystals is a promising strategy for high-performance photothermal materials.

title: Ultrahigh Spatiotemporal Resolution Terahertz Scanning Tunnelling Microscopy
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 02 July 2026;
tldr: This paper reviews terahertz scanning tunnelling microscopy for ultrafast electron dynamics, but does not align with the specified research directions.
motivation: To achieve ultrahigh spatiotemporal resolution for studying ultrafast phenomena in quantum materials.

conclusion: The technique offers insights into ultrafast phenomena and potential advances in quantum materials.

title: Data-driven Discovery Of Dynamical Models In Biology
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 25 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reviews data-driven methods for discovering dynamical models in biology, focusing on regression, network architectures, and decomposition techniques.
motivation: Biological systems often lack known governing equations, so data-driven discovery of dynamical models is needed to understand complex biological processes.
method: The authors compare regression-based methods, network-based architectures, and decomposition techniques for extracting dynamical information from time-resolved data.
result: The review evaluates strengths, limitations, and complementarity of these approaches, providing a guide for selecting appropriate methods.
conclusion: Data-driven discovery is a powerful tool for biological modeling, but careful method selection is crucial based on data characteristics and research questions.

title: Real-space Imaging Of The Electron-pair Density Hole In Molecular Auger–Meitner Decay
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 30 June 2026;
tldr: This paper uses X-ray scattering to image the electron-pair density hole in molecular Auger–Meitner decay.
motivation: Understanding the spatial redistribution of electrons during Auger–Meitner decay is important for molecular physics.
method: Time-resolved X-ray scattering experiments are performed on molecules undergoing Auger–Meitner decay, and the change in electron-pair density is reconstructed.
result: The experiment resolves the spatial redistribution of electrons, providing a real-space picture of the electron-pair density hole.
conclusion: The technique enables direct imaging of electron correlation dynamics in molecular decay processes.

title: Radioactive Molecules As Laboratories Of Fundamental Physics
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 22 June 2026;
tldr: This Perspective discusses the use of radioactive molecules containing octupole-deformed nuclei for precision tests of fundamental physics, such as symmetry violations and new physics beyond the Standard Model.
motivation: To explore new physics at energy scales complementary to high-energy colliders using molecular quantum control.
method: Advances in production, trapping, and quantum control of radioactive molecules are reviewed.
result: Radioactive molecules with octupole-deformed nuclei provide a promising platform for measuring fundamental symmetry violations.
conclusion: These molecular systems can serve as laboratories for fundamental physics, enabling precision tests that are complementary to collider experiments.

title: Harnessing Loss For Q-modulated Biosensors
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 02 July 2026;
tldr: A nanophotonic biosensor using radiative Q-factor modulation in a BIC metasurface for ultrasensitive detection of tumor extracellular vesicles.
motivation: To achieve rapid, label-free, and ultrasensitive detection of disease biomarkers like tumor extracellular vesicles for early diagnosis.
method: Exploits bound states in the continuum (BIC) in a metasurface to convert refractive-index changes into large intensity variations via Q-factor modulation.
result: Demonstrates detection of tens of tumor extracellular vesicles within 15 minutes, showing high sensitivity and scalability.
conclusion: The Q-modulated biosensing strategy offers a promising platform for point-of-care diagnostics with high sensitivity and speed.

method: Seven scientists describe their use of AFM and discuss future directions.
result: A collection of insights on AFM applications and potential advances.
conclusion: AFM remains a versatile tool with many promising avenues for future development.

title: The Physics Of GaN-based Light-emitting Diodes
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 17 June 2026;
tldr: A review of the physics of GaN-based light-emitting diodes, focusing on polarization fields, carrier localization, and non-radiative defects.
motivation: GaN-based LEDs are crucial for modern lighting, and understanding their physics is important for improving efficiency.
method: The review examines three key physical effects: polarization fields, carrier localization, and non-radiative defects.
result: The paper summarizes the current understanding of these effects and their impact on LED performance.
conclusion: Further research is needed to overcome remaining challenges in LED efficiency, particularly related to non-radiative defects.

abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 10 June 2026;

method: The author explains how careful Brillouin spectroscopy can be used to probe lattice dynamics.
result: The technique provides detailed information about lattice dynamics.

title: Non-reciprocal Coalescence-breakup Dynamics In Flowing Concentrated Emulsions
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 06 July 2026;
tldr: This paper studies non-reciprocal coalescence-breakup dynamics in flowing concentrated emulsions using experiments, numerics, and theory.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of concentrated emulsions is important for industrial applications, but catastrophic phase inversion at high volume fractions is poorly understood.
method: The authors combine experimental observations, numerical simulations, and theoretical analysis to investigate the coalescence-breakup dynamics.
result: They reveal critical fluctuations and non-reciprocal behavior in the emulsion dynamics.
conclusion: The study provides new insights into the complex dynamics of concentrated emulsions, which may help control phase inversion in industrial processes.

title: Dielectric-dependent Hybrid Functional Based On meta-GGA
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 04 July 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes a dielectric-dependent hybrid functional based on meta-GGA for accurate energy level calculations in density functional theory.
motivation: Improving the accuracy of electronic structure calculations for materials, particularly energy levels, is important for predicting material properties.
method: The authors develop a hybrid functional that incorporates a modern semilocal meta-GGA exchange-correlation functional and an exact constraint for long-range dielectric screening.
result: The method achieves gold-standard accuracy for energy levels while being computationally efficient and user-friendly.
conclusion: The proposed functional offers a practical and accurate approach for electronic structure calculations in condensed matter physics and materials science.

title: Tricky Tension
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 30 June 2026;
tldr: This paper investigates the microscopic origin of line tension in water nanodroplets on flat surfaces using simulations.

title: Tracking Electrons At The Space-time Limit
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 03 July 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates lightwave-driven scanning tunnelling microscopy with attosecond time resolution to observe individual electrons during tunnelling.
motivation: Understanding electron tunnelling dynamics at the fastest timescales is fundamental to physics and could impact future electronics.
method: The authors use a combination of scanning tunnelling microscopy and attosecond laser pulses to achieve simultaneous spatial and temporal resolution.
result: They successfully track individual electrons as they tunnel through an energy barrier, capturing the process in real time.
conclusion: This technique opens new possibilities for observing ultrafast quantum phenomena at the atomic scale.

title: Self-localization Aids Multiphoton Imaging
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 02 July 2026;
tldr: This paper reports on a self-localization technique that improves multiphoton imaging, a topic in biophotonics.
motivation: Multiphoton imaging suffers from motion artifacts; self-localization can correct for sample movement.
method: The technique uses intrinsic signals from the sample to track and correct motion in real time.
result: Self-localization enables high-resolution imaging without external tracking hardware.
conclusion: This method enhances the practicality of multiphoton microscopy for live tissue imaging.

title: Optical Shaping Of Nanoplasma Shockwaves
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 02 July 2026;

method: The authors use optical pulses to shape the nanoplasma shockwave dynamics, likely through spatial or temporal modulation of the laser field.

title: Relativistic Light Springs Come Into Focus
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 02 July 2026;
tldr: This paper reports the experimental synthesis of relativistic light springs, which are spatio-temporally shaped laser pulses with helical intensity patterns, enabling control over angular momentum in laser-plasma interactions.
motivation: Spatio-temporal shaping of ultra-intense laser pulses is challenging but could unlock new regimes of laser-plasma interactions and control over matter's angular momentum.
method: Researchers synthesized light into a spring-like form at relativistic intensities using spatio-temporal shaping techniques.
result: They demonstrated the generation of relativistic light springs and their potential to control angular momentum degrees of freedom in laser-plasma interactions.
conclusion: This advance may lead to previously unexplored forms of laser-plasma interactions in the laboratory.

title: Visualizing Optical Anisotropy
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 02 July 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a non-interferometric imaging framework for quantitative 3D reconstruction of full dielectric tensors, enabling volumetric measurement of optical anisotropy in complex materials and biological structures.
motivation: Existing methods for measuring optical anisotropy are limited to 2D or require interferometric setups, hindering volumetric characterization of biaxial materials.
method: The authors develop a non-interferometric imaging framework that reconstructs the full dielectric tensor from intensity measurements at multiple illumination angles.
result: The method achieves quantitative 3D reconstruction of biaxial anisotropy in complex materials and biological samples.
conclusion: This work provides a practical route to volumetric optical measurement of anisotropy, with potential applications in materials science and biology.

title: Discovery Is Not The Opposite Of Application
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 30 June 2026;
tldr: This paper argues against framing research funding as a choice between discovery and application, emphasizing that both are complementary.
motivation: The author challenges the false dichotomy between basic and applied research in funding decisions.
method: The paper presents a perspective piece drawing on economic evidence and examples from scientific history.
result: It concludes that discovery and application are not opposites but interdependent, and that funding policies should reflect this.
conclusion: Research funding should support both discovery and application as mutually reinforcing activities.

title: Sub1 Contributes To Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction Driven By Aging In Mice
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 06 July 2026;
tags: heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
tldr: This paper investigates the role of the transcriptional regulator Sub1 in age-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction in mice.
motivation: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) predominantly affects older individuals, and the molecular mechanisms driving age-related HFpEF are poorly understood.
method: The authors used mouse models to study the effects of Sub1 on cardiac function, and performed molecular analyses to examine its interaction with p53 and cardiomyocyte senescence.
result: Sub1 promotes age-related HFpEF in mice, potentially by stabilizing p53 and inducing cardiomyocyte senescence.
conclusion: Sub1 is a key contributor to age-driven HFpEF, suggesting it as a potential therapeutic target.

title: Proton Shuttling At Electrochemical Interfaces Under Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 04 July 2026;
tldr: This paper studies proton shuttling at electrochemical interfaces for alkaline hydrogen evolution, a topic in electrochemistry and materials science.
motivation: Understanding the molecular mechanism of water dissociation in alkaline hydrogen evolution is crucial for improving cost-effective hydrogen production.
method: In-situ spectroscopic observation of proton shuttling in hydration shells of cations.
result: Observation of proton shuttling that can improve water dissociation.
conclusion: The findings provide molecular-level insight into the alkaline hydrogen evolution mechanism.

title: Widespread Controls Of Precipitation Sensitivity On Drought Recovery Of Global Forests
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 04 July 2026;
tldr: This paper studies how precipitation sensitivity affects drought recovery in global forests, an ecological topic unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: Understanding forest recovery after drought is critical for ecosystem resilience under climate change.
method: The authors analyze global forest data to examine the relationship between precipitation sensitivity and drought recovery.
result: Intermediate precipitation sensitivity maximizes drought recovery, while climate-driven increases reduce recovery in many forests.
conclusion: Precipitation sensitivity is a key factor in forest drought recovery, with implications for ecosystem management.

title: The Brca1-a Complex Restricts Replication Fork Reversal-dependent Dna Repair In Atm Deficient Cells
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 04 July 2026;
tldr: This paper studies the role of the BRCA1-A complex in replication fork reversal and DNA repair in ATM-deficient cells, which is a topic in molecular biology and cancer research.
motivation: Understanding how ATM-deficient cells develop chemotherapy resistance is important for cancer treatment.
method: The authors use cellular and molecular biology techniques to investigate the effect of BRCA1-A complex deficiency on replication fork reversal and homologous recombination repair.
result: They find that deficiency in the BRCA1-A complex promotes chemotherapy resistance by restoring fork reversal and enabling homologous recombination repair.
conclusion: The BRCA1-A complex restricts replication fork reversal-dependent DNA repair in ATM-deficient cells, providing a potential target for overcoming chemotherapy resistance.

title: North Pacific Meltwater Weakens The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation And Preconditions Heinrich Stadial 1
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 04 July 2026;
tldr: This paper studies the impact of North Pacific meltwater on the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation during Heinrich Stadial 1, a topic in paleoclimatology.
motivation: To understand the role of Cordilleran ice discharge in triggering AMOC weakening and its connection to Heinrich events.
method: Climate model simulations and proxy data analysis are used to investigate the effects of freshwater input from the North Pacific.
result: North Pacific meltwater discharge can weaken the AMOC and precondition the climate system for Heinrich Stadial 1.
conclusion: The findings suggest a teleconnection between North Pacific freshwater forcing and North Atlantic circulation changes, highlighting the importance of interbasin interactions.

title: Closed-loop Readout Of Anterior Insula High-gamma Activity Steers Value-based Decisions
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 04 July 2026;
tldr: This paper uses a closed-loop intracranial brain-computer interface to show that spontaneous neural fluctuations in the anterior insula can causally influence value-based decisions.
motivation: To understand the causal role of ongoing brain activity in human choice variability, specifically whether spontaneous neural fluctuations can steer value-based decisions.
method: A closed-loop intracranial brain-computer interface was used to read out high-gamma activity from the anterior insula and provide real-time feedback to participants during value-based decision tasks.
result: Spontaneous neural fluctuations in the anterior insula were found to causally shape value-based decisions, demonstrating a direct link between ongoing brain activity and choice variability.
conclusion: Ongoing brain activity in the anterior insula plays a causal role in value-based decision-making, highlighting the importance of neural fluctuations in human choice behavior.
